gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
gaps.explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
gaps.explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you seen my reading glasses?' he asked. He asked ___ his reading glasses.
gaps.explanation: 'If/whether' reports a yes/no question; the tense backshifts to past perfect.
